game: MIA@BUF Week 3 2025 kickoff 2025-09-18 20:15 ET outdoor Buffalo closing spread -12.5 total 50.5 implied BUF 31.5 MIA 19.0

script.base: Thursday night outdoor at Buffalo, closing line Bills -12.5 and total 50.5 (nflverse games.csv), so the book expects Buffalo to lead and both teams to score (BUF 31.5, MIA 19.0). Base flow: Buffalo is ahead by halftime, Josh Allen keeps a designed-run share (16 carries, 95 yards in weeks 1-2) but James Cook (34 carries, 176 yards) is the closer who kills the clock. Miami trails with a 19-point implied total and throws: Tyreek Hill (13 targets, 211 air yards) and De'Von Achane (14 targets, -12 air yards, 112 receiving yards) stay involved, while Ollie Gordon (3 carries, 12 yards) does not take the early-down job. Pace is not a slog because 50.5 is a high total, but the split tilts Buffalo run and Miami pass as the lead grows.
script.flip1: Blowout: Buffalo is up three scores by half. Starter snaps get cut after the clock-kill, so Cook can stall late and Ray Davis (10 carries, rush games of 2 and 24) mops up, while Miami either dumps to Achane and Hill in garbage time or the drive count dies if Tua is off the field. That is the snap-risk flag on a 12.5-point spread.
script.flip2: Miami hangs around because Ed Oliver is out and the total is 50.5, and it becomes a stay-in-it or shootout game. Both passing games stay live, Achane keeps a full rush-plus-receiving role, Cook never gets a pure carry bump, and Buffalo WR yards do not stall. A second environment flip is weather dragging the outdoor total, but no forecast was saved.

injury_fallout: Source is the pre-game nflverse injury report, not inactives. Buffalo: LB Matt Milano Out (pectoral) and DT Ed Oliver Out (ankle); LB Shaq Thompson (hamstring), CB Taron Johnson (quad) and CB Cam Lewis (shoulder) are Questionable only. Milano out is a linebacker void for Achane checkdowns; Oliver out weakens the interior front that would stuff runs and the rush that would punish Tua, who already has a -1.10 EPA per dropback when blitzed. If Johnson or Lewis sit, Hill and Waddle coverage thins, but that is not confirmed. Miami: TE Darren Waller Out (hip) and already absent from the weeks 1-2 target list, so the short-area leftovers are Alec Ingold (4 targets, 14 yards) and T.Conner (4 targets, 20 yards), not a new tight-end prop. WR Jaylen Waddle is Questionable (shoulder) with 11 targets, 98 yards and 119 air yards (games 30 and 68); if he is inactive, Hill (13 targets) and Malik Washington (7 targets, 22 yards, games 20 and 2) absorb, but that is a game-time decision. S Ifeatu Melifonwu Out (calf) and CB Storm Duck Out (ankle) thin the secondary Keon Coleman (158 air yards) and Josh Palmer (162 air yards) would attack. DT Benito Jones (oblique) and LB Chop Robinson (knee) are Questionable on the front Cook would run at. Final inactives about 90 minutes before kickoff are not in the pack.

matchup.shell: Middle-of-field open versus closed and man-versus-zone rates are not in the pack, so shell charting is unavailable. What is known: Buffalo blitzes 36 percent and Miami blitzes 43 percent. Zone-versus-man mapping of Hill, Waddle, Coleman, Palmer, Shakir and Kincaid to specific corners cannot be done from this pack.
matchup.pressure: Buffalo blitz rate 36 percent meets a Miami offense that is -1.10 EPA per dropback when blitzed and +0.19 when not, so pressure that gets home kills Tyreek Hill deep yards (211 air yards on 13 targets) and Jaylen Waddle (119 air yards). The same pressure rule boosts running-back and tight-end catches; Achane is already the negative-air target (14 targets, -12 air, 112 receiving yards). Miami blitzes 43 percent and Buffalo is +0.91 EPA per dropback versus the blitz against +0.19 with no blitz, so Allen beats extra rushers rather than only checking down, which supports team scoring but does not force Dalton Kincaid or Cook screens.
matchup.bleeds: Buffalo's run defense is the bleed: 6.76 yards per carry allowed and 14 runs of 10-plus in two games. Their pass defense is uneven, left 4.73 YPA on 11 attempts, middle 9.8 on 10, right 7.1 on 20, and only 5 gains of 20-plus for 47 yards, so explosives have not been the leak. Miami's run defense does not bleed: 4.26 yards per carry and 9 runs of 10-plus. Miami's pass defense does bleed: left 8.81 YPA on 27 attempts, middle 8.8 on 5, right 11.0 on 20, plus 6 gains of 20-plus for 56 yards, with Melifonwu and Storm Duck already out.
matchup.overlap: The overlap being bet is Achane, 18 carries and 85 rush yards plus 14 targets, into Buffalo's 6.76 YPC run leak, Oliver out, and the Milano linebacker void, on the rush-plus-receiving market so a trailing script does not kill the leg by itself. Cook is the script overlap, lead back into a Buffalo lead, not a run-defense overlap, because Miami allows 4.26 YPC. Not selected: Hill's 211 air yards into a Buffalo defense with only 5 explosives and a blitz that has produced -1.10 EPA for Miami; Coleman and Palmer air yards into Miami's 11.0 right-side YPA is real but fights the clock-kill base script.

form: Only weeks 1-2 are in the pack, not a 3-4 game sample, and there is no noted OC or QB change. Achane rush yards 55 then 30 (18 carries, 85 yards, 4.72 YPC), receiving 20 then 92 (14 targets, 112 yards), rush-plus-rec 75 then 122. Cook rush 44 then 132 on 34 carries and 176 yards (5.18 YPC), receiving 58 then 3. Coleman 112 then 26 on 14 targets and 158 air yards. Hill 40 then 109. Palmer is the stable Buffalo receiver at 61 and 47. Shakir 64 then 12. Kincaid 48 then 37, with Dawson Knox also at 7 targets and 39 yards. Davis 2 then 24 rush yards. Gordon 4 then 8. The 132-yard Cook game and the 112-yard Coleman game look spike-like next to 44 and 26, but play-by-play is not in the pack so they are not marked as one-play flukes.

pro_edge.implied_totals: Favorite Buffalo 31.5 and dog Miami 19.0, from (50.5+12.5)/2 and (50.5-12.5)/2, matching the precomputed pro-edge block. High total means more plays and a volume lean; the 12.5 spread means the dog throws more and the leader runs late, with a blowout flag on starter snaps.
pro_edge.script_read: Buffalo should lead and hand Cook the late carries; Miami should trail and raise Achane, Hill and Waddle targets. A three-score lead would shift late carries toward Ray Davis (line 13.5, games 2 and 24) and could cut Allen and Coleman volume. All prop numbers in the pack are 2-game stand-in medians, not live shopped lines, so they have not absorbed Oliver, Milano, Melifonwu or Duck.
pro_edge.best_price: No two-sided price was saved on Cook rush 88.5, Cook rush-plus-rec 118.5, Cook receiving 30.5, Achane rush 42.5, Achane receiving 56.5, Achane rush-plus-rec 98.5, Hill 74.5, Waddle 49.5, Coleman 69.5, Palmer 54.5, Shakir 38.5, Kincaid 42.5, Davis, Gordon or Washington. Anchor no-vig fair is N/A. No Pinnacle, Circa or BetOnline price beats an anchor because no book price exists.
pro_edge.lagging: No lagging-line flag. The pack has the nflverse closing spread and total only, no open, and no book-level props that failed to move after the number. Stand-in medians cannot lag.
pro_edge.sleepers: Ruled out: Milano, Oliver, Waller (already missing from Miami targets), Melifonwu, Duck. Questionable, not out, so not a full sleeper trigger: Waddle, Thompson, Taron Johnson, Cam Lewis, Benito Jones, Chop Robinson. Same-position lines are unadjusted stand-ins: Waddle questionable points at Washington receiving 11.5 (games 20 and 2) and Hill 74.5; Waller out has no Miami tight-end prop, with Ingold and Conner the tiny shares; Milano and Oliver out leave Achane 42.5, 56.5 and 98.5 unmoved; Melifonwu and Duck out leave Coleman 69.5, Palmer 54.5, Shakir 38.5 and Kincaid 42.5 unmoved. Treat those as low-confidence personnel notes, not bettable prices.

pre_mortem: It is Monday and both legs lost. Cook rush over lost because Miami's front, 4.26 yards per carry and 9 runs of 10-plus, held him to the 44-yard script, Allen kept the 8-carry rushing share, and a late lead went to Ray Davis instead of extra Cook carries, so 88.5 was just the average of a spike and a dud. Achane rush-plus-rec over lost because Buffalo blitzed an offense at -1.10 EPA per dropback, Hill and a healthy Waddle took the trailing targets, and Achane finished near 30 rush and 20 receiving while Gordon took garbage carries, repeating 75 instead of 122. The Buffalo 6.76 YPC and 14 explosives were a two-game sample that did not travel. Those counters are why Cook is flagged rather than sized and Achane stays a lean; they are not stronger than the lead-back clock-kill read or the two-path Achane read, so neither leg is cut.
slip_story: One script stack, not a mixed slip: Buffalo leads on the road favorite side of a 50.5 total, Cook rush over is the clock-kill anchor, and Achane rush-plus-rec over is the trailing-dog usage leg that still has a soft Buffalo front if the game stays competitive. They can win together in the base script. Do not add a total under, a Buffalo WR over, Coleman or Palmer under, Achane rush-only, or a second market on either player. No touchdown legs. Waddle is left off because he is Questionable. Prices were never available, so this is a read for the human, not a placed bet.
